messages.subject: Single visit
parts:
Hello Unmarked group,

I'm trying to compare "historical" versus "current" distribution of birds using single-season occupancy models using "ERA" as a covariate ( sites are not the same between ERAs).

The current dataset consists of 99 sampling sites. The historical dataset includes 73 sampling sites, but 22 of these sampling sites were sampled only once ( single visit).  I would like to keep these 22 sites in the analyses because I do have information from these sites for the "Current ERA". 

 If I keep these 22 sites the uncertainty in the occupancy and detection parameters will increase and preclude my comparison of occupancy between ERAs?

Thanks

Best

Marconi

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Single visit
parts:
Dear Marconi,

 

I would keep them in and don’t think that there is any problem. They add information and this will be used in the analysis, though almost all of the information about p will come from those sites where you do have replication. This will then be propagated also for estimation with these 22 sites.

 

This approach assumes that these 22 sites are a random sample of all sites and not in some way systematically different. In the latter case, I would throw them out, because the info about p coming from the sites with replication might not be pertinent to them.

 

Best regards  --  Marc
